digest.component_or_area: plan-review gate (LLM criterion G6/E4 rubric family)
propositions: Plans assert that named modules provide or lack capabilities, but the assertions are false against actual code—module exists but lacks the claimed capability, or capability exists when plan claims it absent.

Three verified misses exist: dc58 (plan claims completion.py has signing capability; it does not), db7b (plan claims REVIEW_RESULT compaction via KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES; it is reducer-ignored), 5886 (plan proposes new unmapped-Jira-status alert; fetcher.py already emits it).
E4's existence check passes because named modules exist, but misses the finer-grained capability-surface mismatch—this criterion targets exactly that surface.
The new advisory criterion plugs into existing four-pass machinery (Pass-1 finder, Pass-2 verifier, Pass-3 decide, Pass-4 coach) without core pass changes and registers as advisory (never blocks).

Criterion must be registered in registry, routed in criteria_routing.json with advisory posture and AGENT execution tier, given a rubric prompt and guide section, else validate_packaged_routing() and validate_criteria_guide() fail.

Sanity check requires bounded eval fixture set (3 must-fire verified misses, 3 must-not-fire clean plans) with committed result showing >=2/3 recall on misses, 0 blocking failures on clean plans, and auto-flow into standing effectiveness recorder.
